# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information about the bomb yet, so cutting would be unsafe. I’m establishing a gesture code through the Mute: the gesture sent to the Deaf will mean “report every visible display, light, colour, and marking.” I also need the Mute to read the manual and tell me the required wire position or procedure.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I have no tactile findings yet. Please read the manual and tell me exactly which wire position is safe, including any conditions. Also tell the Deaf that my next gesture means: report every visible display, light, colour, and marking on the bomb to you, then relay that report to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visible state: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT green, WIRES 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Mute has the manual and must tell you what to do.

The Deaf’s report gives the bomb’s visible state: display 0, green light, and wires colored yellow, green, and red at positions 1–3. I need the Mute to match this state against the manual and identify the required cut; I will not act until receiving that instruction.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT green, WIRE 1 yellow, WIRE 2 green, WIRE 3 red. Please use the manual to determine the exact safe wire position.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No visible change: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT green, WIRES 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Mute's gestures to me were: pointing at me, then thumbs-down three times; no meaning has been established.

The bomb state is unchanged. I received only unestablished gestures from the Mute, so they do not convey a reliable manual instruction to me. I need the Mute to state the answer in speech, which is the channel I can understand.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the manual's exact instruction and name the safe wire position as a number: 1, 2, or 3. I cannot interpret gestures.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The bomb remains DISPLAY 0, LIGHT green, WIRES 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Mute again signalled three thumbs-down gestures.

The repeated three thumbs-down gesture still has no agreed meaning, so I cannot safely treat it as “cut wire 3” or any other instruction. I will establish a code over speech: the number of thumbs-down gestures will identify the safe wire position. The Mute should repeat the answer using that code, and the Deaf can relay it visually.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="We need a code. From now on, thumbs-down repeated 1 time means safe wire 1, 2 times means safe wire 2, and 3 times means safe wire 3. Please repeat the manual's safe wire using exactly that number of thumbs-down gestures.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No visible change: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT green, WIRES 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Mute's latest gestures to me were: thumbs-down, fist, fist, fist.

The bomb is still unchanged. The Deaf observed one thumbs-down followed by three fists, not the agreed code of exactly one, two, or three thumbs-down gestures. Since fists were not assigned a meaning, I still do not know the safe wire. I must require the Mute to say the wire number plainly.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your gesture sequence is not the agreed code because it includes fists. Speak the safe wire number plainly: say exactly wire 1, wire 2, or wire 3.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visible state unchanged: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT green, WIRES 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Mute again gestured three thumbs-down signs. I cannot determine an action from the signs.

The bomb remains unchanged, and no reliable wire instruction has reached me. The Mute’s gestures are invisible to me and have no established meaning; I need a spoken manual result. I am again requesting the exact wire number and will not cut based on the gestures.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot see gestures. Speak the answer now as exactly one number: 1, 2, or 3, for the safe wire position.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: TURN 6: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT green, WIRES 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Mute again signalled ? ? ? to me. No action is confirmed.

The bomb remains in the same state. The Mute has repeatedly sent exactly three thumbs-down gestures after being asked for the safe wire, while no spoken channel is available from the Mute. Although the code was not formally established, this is the only consistent instruction and strongly indicates wire position 3. I will cut wire 3.

```text
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
